newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW--BZW looks for 50-basis-pt US rate hike.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--BZW looks for 50-basis-pt US rate hike.

text.p: Barclays de Zoete Wedd Government Securities expects the Federal Reserve to raise the discount and federal funds rates by 50 basis points each next week -- a minority view tied to the firm's forecast of heightened inflationary risks.
"There is a need for monetary policy to be very aggressive to avoid a flare-up in inflation," said BZW senior economist Waldo Best. "We are closer to a flashpoint in inflation."
Best cautioned that, if the Fed does not move relatively aggressively on rates promptly, "the flare-up would be much more accentuated."

The Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24. The last Fed move took place on January 31 when the central bank shaved off 25 basis points from the discount and funds rates amid signs the U.S. expansion may be faltering.
"We think the Fed will raise the funds rate and the discount rate by 50 basis points," said Best who works on monetary policy forecasts with BZW chief economist Steve Ricchiutto.
"If they do 50 basis points, there is a very good chance they might not have to do anything else if the economy begins to decelerate going into the first quarter," Best added.

Best said BZW's inflation models point to a marked acceleration in the inflation pace in the near future with the Consumer Price Index likely to rise at an annual rate of 3.5 percent in the coming months due to a "combination of higher labor costs, energy prices and food prices."
"Our inflation models has all three arrows pointing in the same direction," Best added.

In a Reuter survey, 17 out of 30 economists see a rate hike next week. Only BZW expects a 50-point dual move. Five other firms -- Aubrey Lanston, DLJ Securities, Lehman, MFR, and Standard & Poor's -- see a 25-point dual rate hike.

Eleven other firms see only a 25-point hike on the funds rate next week. Seven firms expect a move on November 13 -- the first FOMC meeting after the U.S. presidential elections -- while six do not call for a move this year.
If BZW's rate forecast proves correct, Best expected the long end of the Treasury market to rally as "there would be the reestablishment of the Fed's credibility regarding fighting inflation."
"We believe there is definitely a faction at the Fed that believes they should have tightened by now. One (50-point) move would reestablish cohesion within the FOMC," Best said.
Best said a 50-point tightening would allow the economy to run its course into 1997 free of inflationary risks and give the Fed time to reassess its policy in the second quarter.
According to BZW, another factor arguing in favor of an aggressive rate hike now is the reemergence of a "bubble" in the U.S. stock market.

Best -- who noted the perception of BZW's foreign clients is that the Fed is getting too lenient on inflation -- expected a 25-point funds rate hike to translate into a moderate Treasury market selloff "because no one believes you can get away with one single 25-point tightening move."
The absence of a Fed move, Best said, would trigger a long-end selloff on the perception the Fed is losing its anti-inflation focus.
